action_attack.name: Attack
action_attack.narrative: The fundamental act of violence in the galaxy - whether with blaster, blade, or bare hands. Every sentient being learns to defend themselves, but true masters turn attack into an art form. From the precise strikes of a Jedi Guardian to the brutal efficiency of a Mandalorian warrior, the way one attacks reveals their training, culture, and philosophy.
action_attack.flavor_text: 'The best defense is a swift and decisive offense.' - Ancient Mandalorian proverb
action_attack.cultural_significance: Different cultures view attack differently - Jedi see it as a last resort, Mandalorians as honorable combat, bounty hunters as business, and criminals as survival. The method and style of attack often reveals more about the attacker than the target.
action_attack.description: Make a weapon attack against a target within range. Roll to hit, then roll damage if successful.
action_attack.action_process: Choose a target within your weapon's range, make an attack roll using your weapon's attack bonus, and if successful, roll damage dice to determine the harm inflicted.
action_attack.origin_story: The concept of attack predates recorded history, evolving from basic survival instincts into sophisticated martial arts and combat techniques across countless species and cultures.

connections.narrative: Jedi Guardians are masters of lightsaber combat, turning the basic attack into a flowing dance of defense and offense.
connections.mechanical_benefit: Guardians gain additional attack options and defensive capabilities

connections.narrative: Bounty Hunters specialize in precise, efficient attacks designed to quickly neutralize targets.
connections.mechanical_benefit: Bounty Hunters gain advantage on attack rolls against marked targets

connections.narrative: Mandalorian culture places great emphasis on martial prowess, with attack techniques passed down through generations.
connections.mechanical_benefit: Mandalorians gain proficiency with all weapons

connections.narrative: The Jedi Order teaches that attack should only be used in defense of life and justice, never in anger or aggression.
connections.mechanical_benefit: Jedi gain access to special defensive attack techniques

iconic_examples: Obi-Wan Kenobi's defensive stance against Darth Vader
famous_instances: The Battle of Geonosis - first major battle of the Clone Wars
The Siege of Mandalore - Ahsoka's final confrontation with Maul
The Battle of Endor - the final assault on the Death Star II

narrative_hooks: A character's attack style reveals their training and background
The choice of weapon and attack method can create interesting social dynamics
Different cultures may react differently to certain types of attacks
adventure_seeds: A master of a unique attack style seeks an apprentice

llm_guidance.cultural_impact: Attack methods and philosophies vary greatly across the galaxy, from the disciplined forms of the Jedi to the brutal efficiency of criminal organizations. These differences often lead to cultural misunderstandings and conflicts.
llm_guidance.tactical_significance: The choice of when and how to attack is often more important than the attack itself. Timing, positioning, and understanding your opponent's capabilities are crucial for success.

sandbox_campaignstate.narrative: In the fragile calm after Endor, power vacuums breed new predators. Imperial warlords, Hutt syndicates, and shadowy Force sects maneuver across the Rim, each seeking advantage as worlds try to rebuild. The party is drawn into a web of espionage, clandestine raids, and moral compromises—where the line between justice and vengeance blurs and every alliance has a price.
sandbox_campaignstate.flavor_text: "Victory rarely feels like peace. It feels like the moment you realize someone else has already started the next war."
sandbox_campaignstate.cultural_significance: For frontier worlds, this era is defined by pragmatic survival and shifting loyalties. On Core Worlds, politics is theater layered over quiet purges and reconciliations. For Force traditions, the era is an open question: could something more nuanced than Jedi vs. Sith take root?
sandbox_campaignstate.description: A mid-length campaign focused on dismantling an Imperial remnant cell that has infiltrated trade routes, seized hidden depots, and weaponized local criminal networks. Operations mix heists, diplomacy, and targeted strikes.
sandbox_campaignstate.origin_story: An encrypted Rebel-era asset registry surfaces, pointing to a missing logistics node once overseen by a ruthless Imperial quartermaster. The registry is incomplete, but a pattern of false manifests and dead drops suggests an ongoing operation.

current_session.session_summary: The party traced falsified cargo tags to a decommissioned listening post on Vardos' dark side. They exfiltrated intel but drew the attention of local enforcers.

sandbox_campaignstate.campaign_notes: The quartermaster uses plausible deniability, subcontractors, and cut-outs. They prefer to ruin reputations before striking.
sandbox_campaignstate.next_session_prep: Prep a tense negotiation at a neutral bazaar; introduce a mysterious droid broker who trades in memories.

connections.narrative: Imperial loyalists fund, arm, and protect the remnant cell.
Echoes of the past haunt the few who still speak of the Jedi.

llm_guidance.roleplay_guidance: Keep tension high by showing costs—civilian fear, indebted allies, and fragile truces. Offer moral choices that trade speed for integrity.
narrative_hooks: A coded plea from a Rebel-era ally who vanished after Endor resurfaces.
A Hutt kajidic offers intel that would topple a remnant node—for a price.
A Force-sensitive orphan exhibits strange instincts that unsettle the party.
A New Republic audit uncovers the party's forged manifests.
llm_guidance.social_dynamics: Allies expect reciprocity; informants demand protection; local leaders fear becoming the next proxy battlefield.
llm_guidance.campaign_development: Start with intel-gathering and small strikes. Escalate to supply-chain disruption and leadership decapitation. End with exposing the quartermaster and forcing a public reckoning.

guardian.flavor_text: A Jedi uses the Force for knowledge and defense, never for attack. - Yoda

creature_shadowstalker_nexu.name: Shadowstalker Nexu
creature_shadowstalker_nexu.narrative: A lean, void-black subspecies of nexu adapted for urban predation. Bred by clandestine Imperial kennels for silence, obedience, and terror operations, Shadowstalkers slip through vents and scaffolds like liquid night. Their whisker-spines sense air pressure and sound, letting them hunt in total darkness. A single hissing exhale often precedes the strike.
creature_shadowstalker_nexu.flavor_text: "You never see the first one. You hear the second—and realize the first is behind you." — Anonymous dockside rumor, Level 1313
creature_shadowstalker_nexu.cultural_significance: On lower levels, the Shadowstalker is a cautionary tale—proof that empires engineer monsters on purpose. On imperial black-sites, they are an asset classed as both deterrent and disposal.
creature_shadowstalker_nexu.description: Quadrupedal ambush predator with retractable talons, split jaws, and low infrared signature. Uses verticality and blind angles to isolate prey.
creature_shadowstalker_nexu.origin_story: Gene-edited from captured nexu stock and trained with shock-collar conditioning. A handful escaped into megastructure undercities.

attacks.name: Silent Pounce

attacks.special: On hit, the target takes an additional 1d4 damage at the start of its next turn.

creature_shadowstalker_nexu.ai_behavior: Avoids open light, splits the party, retreats after a hard hit, then re-engages from a new angle. Targets the isolated and the loud first.

connections.narrative: Used for intimidation and deniable disappearances in occupied sectors.

llm_guidance.roleplay_guidance: Play the environment against the players: flickering lights, steam vents, narrow gantries. Describe breathy hisses from multiple directions to seed paranoia. Let silence build before you break it.
narrative_hooks: A black-market handler offers a bounty for a live capture—no questions.
A labor union blames management for weaponizing predators to break strikes.
A fallen ISB tech wants to trade den site coordinates for extraction.
llm_guidance.social_dynamics: Locals share whispered routes and talismanic wards; enforcers deny the problem to avoid panic.
llm_guidance.creature_development: Escalate from single ambushes to coordinated pack tactics as the pack learns the party's rhythms.

wookiee.flavor_text: Wookiees are known for their deep connection to the natural world, and their reverence for the ancient forest moon of Kashyyyk. Their culture is built upon a profound respect for life, honor, and family - principles that guide them in all aspects of their lives. As a Wookiee, you embody these values, and your actions are shaped by the unwavering commitment to protect and preserve the balance of nature.

llm_guidance.roleplay_guidance: As a Wookiee, you have an innate sense of loyalty and duty. You prioritize family and tribe above all else, and will go to great lengths to defend and support those you care about. However, this strong sense of allegiance can sometimes lead to blind spots and conflicts with others who do not share your values or priorities. Be mindful of this tendency, and strive to find a balance between loyalty and self-awareness.
narrative_hooks: Explore the complexities of Wookiee honor culture
Delve into the ancient history of Kashyyyk and its impact on modern Wookiee society
llm_guidance.social_dynamics: Wookiees are known for their close-knit family bonds, but this also means they can be fiercely protective and sometimes isolationist. Be prepared to navigate these dynamics when interacting with other species or individuals who may not understand or respect Wookiee customs.

"A Wookiee is a skilled melee fighter, relying on its strength and agility to take down opponents.

ai_behavior.social_behavior:
"A Wookiee values building strong relationships through shared experiences and mutual respect.

Their culture is built upon a profound respect for life, honor, and family - principles that guide them in all aspects of their lives. As a Wookiee, you embody these values, and your actions are shaped by the unwavering commitment to protect and preserve the balance of nature.

llm_guidance.roleplay_guidance: As a Wookiee, you have an innate sense of loyalty and duty. You prioritize family and tribe above all else, and will go to great lengths to defend and support those you care about. However, this strong sense of allegiance can sometimes lead to blind spots and conflicts with others who do not share your values or priorities. Be mindful of this tendency, and strive to find a balance between loyalty and self-awareness.

llm_guidance.social_dynamics: Wookiees are known for their close-knit family bonds, but this also means they can be fiercely protective and sometimes isolationist. lore_coruscant.name: Coruscant
lore_coruscant.narrative: Coruscant is the crown jewel of the galaxy, a planet-wide city that serves as the political, economic, and cultural heart of the Republic. Once a world of natural beauty, it has been completely covered by a vast urban sprawl that reaches thousands of levels into the sky. The planet's surface is hidden beneath layers of durasteel and transparisteel, with only the peaks of ancient mountains still visible as the tips of the tallest skyscrapers. Coruscant represents the pinnacle of civilization and the center of galactic power, but also the corruption and decadence that can come with such concentrated wealth and influence.
lore_coruscant.flavor_text: 'If there's a bright center to the universe, you're on the planet that it's farthest from.' - Luke Skywalker
lore_coruscant.cultural_significance: Coruscant is viewed as the ultimate symbol of civilization and progress by most galactic citizens, though some see it as a monument to excess and corruption. It represents the dream of a unified galaxy and the reality of bureaucratic inefficiency.

description.text: Coruscant is a terrestrial planet located in the Core Worlds, completely covered by a planet-wide city. The planet's surface is hidden beneath thousands of levels of urban development, with only the ancient mountain peaks still visible as the tips of the tallest buildings. The planet has a temperate climate maintained by advanced environmental systems, and its atmosphere is carefully regulated to support the massive population.

SECRET: Beneath the gleaming towers of Galactic City lies a vast network of ancient tunnels and chambers, some dating back to the earliest days of galactic civilization. These underground levels contain forgotten temples, ancient archives, and mysterious artifacts that hint at Coruscant's true origins.

FORBIDDEN: Deep within the planet's core, ancient texts speak of a Sith shrine built by a fallen Jedi Master centuries before the Clone Wars. This shrine was deliberately buried beneath the Jedi Temple, creating a dark nexus that influenced generations of Jedi and ultimately contributed to their downfall.

lore_coruscant.physical_description: A planet-sized city with thousands of levels of urban development. The surface is completely covered by buildings, streets, and infrastructure. The tallest buildings reach several kilometers into the sky, and the lowest levels extend deep into the planet's crust. The planet has a temperate climate maintained by advanced environmental systems, with artificial weather patterns and carefully regulated atmosphere.

historical_context.text: Originally a world of natural beauty with mountains, oceans, and diverse ecosystems, Coruscant was gradually developed over millennia as the center of galactic civilization. The planet's transformation began during the early days of space travel and accelerated during the formation of the Galactic Republic. By the time of the Clone Wars, the entire planet had been covered by urban development.

HIDDEN: The Jedi Temple was built on the site of an ancient Sith shrine, a fact known only to the highest-ranking Jedi Masters. This dark influence subtly affected the Jedi Order for generations, contributing to their eventual fall.

lore_coruscant.current_status: During the Galactic Republic era, Coruscant serves as the capital and seat of government. The planet is home to the Jedi Temple, the Senate Building, and countless government offices, corporate headquarters, and residential districts. It remains the most important world in the galaxy.

wookiee__species.flavor_text: Wookiees are known for their deep connection to the natural world, and their reverence for the ancient forest moon of Kashyyyk. Their culture is built upon a profound respect for life, honor, and family - principles that guide them in all aspects of their lives. As a Wookiee, you embody these values, and your actions are shaped by the unwavering commitment to protect and preserve the balance of nature.

llm_guidance.roleplay_guidance: As a Wookiee, you have an innate sense of loyalty and duty. You prioritize family and tribe above all else, and will go to great lengths to defend and support those you care about. However, this strong sense of allegiance can sometimes lead to blind spots and conflicts with others who do not share your values or priorities. Be mindful of this tendency, and strive to find a balance between loyalty and self-awareness.
narrative_hooks: Explore the complexities of Wookiee honor culture

starship_millennium_falcon.narrative: The Millennium Falcon is one of the most famous starships in the galaxy, a heavily modified YT-1300 light freighter that has become a symbol of hope and rebellion. Originally a standard Corellian freighter, the ship has been extensively customized by its various owners, particularly Han Solo and Chewbacca, who transformed it into a fast, well-armed vessel capable of outrunning Imperial patrols and surviving dangerous missions. The Falcon's distinctive dish-shaped sensor array and battered exterior hide a ship that has seen countless adventures and saved the galaxy multiple times.

starship_millennium_falcon.cultural_significance: The Millennium Falcon represents the spirit of freedom and rebellion against tyranny. To the Empire, it's a notorious smuggler's ship and a symbol of resistance. To the Rebellion, it's a beacon of hope and proof that even the smallest ship can make a difference. Throughout the galaxy, the Falcon's distinctive silhouette is recognized as a sign that help is on the way, or that trouble is about to arrive.

The Falcon's distinctive round sensor dish and asymmetrical design make it instantly recognizable.
starship_millennium_falcon.physical_description: The Millennium Falcon is a roughly cylindrical freighter with a distinctive round sensor dish mounted on the starboard side. The ship's exterior is covered in dents, scratches, and carbon scoring from countless battles and close calls. The main hull is approximately 34.75 meters long, with a width of 25.61 meters. The ship's design is asymmetrical, with the cockpit offset to the port side and various protrusions and modifications visible on the hull. The landing gear consists of three retractable struts, and the ship has multiple access hatches and maintenance panels.

subclass_guardian_protector.narrative: You are the ultimate guardian, a living shield whose very presence creates a sanctuary of safety. Your mastery of protective techniques goes beyond mere defense—you become an extension of the Force itself, creating an impenetrable barrier between your charges and any threat that would harm them.
subclass_guardian_protector.flavor_text: 'I will not let harm come to those under my protection. The Force flows through me to shield them.' - A Guardian Protector

subclass_identity_profile.core_fantasy: Unwavering guardians of the innocent, Protectors wield their lightsabers with precision and power.

llm_guidance.roleplay_guidance: Protectors are defined by their unwavering commitment to others' safety. They should always be thinking about how to position themselves to protect their charges, and their actions should reflect this protective mindset. They are calm under pressure, always ready to sacrifice themselves for others, and have an almost supernatural ability to sense danger before it strikes.
narrative_hooks: The Protector must choose between protecting their assigned charge and saving innocent civilians caught in the crossfire.
A powerful enemy specifically targets the Protector's charge, testing their defensive abilities to the limit.
The Protector discovers a plot that threatens not just their charge, but the entire organization they serve.
The Protector's charge is kidnapped, and they must use all their skills to track and rescue them.
llm_guidance.tactical_notes: Protectors excel at positioning and defensive tactics. They should always be thinking about how to create protective barriers, intercept attacks, and ensure their charges' safety. Their abilities work best when they can focus on protecting specific individuals rather than trying to protect everyone at once.

progression_tree.description: As a Protector, you can enter a defensive stance at the start of your turn, granting you advantage on all Intimidation checks and allowing you to move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

You can use your reaction to deflect one attack roll against you this turn. The attacker must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC of 15 + your proficiency bonus. On a successful save, the attack is deflected and has no effect.

When a friendly creature within 10 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to grant them a bonus to their Armor Class until the start of your next turn. The bonus is equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum +1).

As a Protector, you can enter an unyielding stance at the start of your turn. Until the start of your next turn, you have advantage on all Strength checks and can move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

You can use your action to generate a shield around yourself, granting you a bonus to your Armor Class equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum +1). The shield lasts for 1 minute and can be dispelled by any effect that deals radiant damage.

dynamic_visuals.combat_stance: Assuming a defensive stance with feet shoulder-width apart and lightsaber held at a 45-degree angle, ready to strike at a moment's notice.
dynamic_visuals.energy_signature: A vibrant blue aura surrounds the Protector's body, pulsing with energy as they channel their connection to the Force.

campaign.narrative: In the fragile calm after Endor, power vacuums breed new predators. Imperial warlords, Hutt syndicates, and shadowy Force sects maneuver across the Rim, each seeking advantage as worlds try to rebuild. The party is drawn into a web of espionage, clandestine raids, and moral compromises—where the line between justice and vengeance blurs and every alliance has a price.
campaign.flavor_text: "Victory rarely feels like peace. It feels like the moment you realize someone else has already started the next war."
campaign.cultural_significance: For frontier worlds, this era is defined by pragmatic survival and shifting loyalties. On Core Worlds, politics is theater layered over quiet purges and reconciliations. For Force traditions, the era is an open question: could something more nuanced than Jedi vs. Sith take root?
campaign.description: A mid-length campaign focused on dismantling an Imperial remnant cell that has infiltrated trade routes, seized hidden depots, and weaponized local criminal networks. Operations mix heists, diplomacy, and targeted strikes.
campaign.origin_story: An encrypted Rebel-era asset registry surfaces, pointing to a missing logistics node once overseen by a ruthless Imperial quartermaster. The registry is incomplete, but a pattern of false manifests and dead drops suggests an ongoing operation.

current_session.session_summary: The party traced falsified cargo tags to a decommissioned listening post on Vardos' dark side. They exfiltrated intel but drew the attention of local enforcers.

campaign.campaign_notes: The quartermaster uses plausible deniability, subcontractors, and cut-outs. They prefer to ruin reputations before striking.
campaign.next_session_prep: Prep a tense negotiation at a neutral bazaar; introduce a mysterious droid broker who trades in memories.

connections.narrative: Imperial loyalists fund, arm, and protect the remnant cell.
Echoes of the past haunt the few who still speak of the Jedi.

llm_guidance.roleplay_guidance: Keep tension high by showing costs—civilian fear, indebted allies, and fragile truces. Offer moral choices that trade speed for integrity.
narrative_hooks: A coded plea from a Rebel-era ally who vanished after Endor resurfaces.
A Hutt kajidic offers intel that would topple a remnant node—for a price.
A Force-sensitive orphan exhibits strange instincts that unsettle the party.
A New Republic audit uncovers the party's forged manifests.
llm_guidance.social_dynamics: Allies expect reciprocity; informants demand protection; local leaders fear becoming the next proxy battlefield.
llm_guidance.campaign_development: Start with intel-gathering and small strikes. Escalate to supply-chain disruption and leadership decapitation. End with exposing the quartermaster and forcing a public reckoning.

image_generation.base_prompt: A wide cinematic matte painting of a clandestine operation underway in a starport carved into a canyon on a remote Rim world at dusk. Smugglers and saboteurs move through harsh light and deep shadow between cargo silhouettes and scaffolded gantries. A New Republic corvette hangs low overhead, lights off, while a disguised Imperial shuttle loads contraband below. Tension in the air, dust, exhaust haze, hard rim lighting, moody color grading, high-detail concept art, gritty realism.

contextual_modifiers.modifier_text: Include a subtle Imperial cog spray-painted over with New Republic insignia; suggest contested authority and uneasy transition.
Emphasize silhouettes, angled light beams, and a single orange pauldron in the crowd as a threat motif.
